name: Sweden
summary: Stockholm's exchange has traded since 4 February 1863 and is now Nasdaq Stockholm, part of Nasdaq's Nordic markets. The OMXS30 holds 30 large Swedish companies, many of them industrial groups, and many Swedish companies list separate A and B share classes. Shares trade in Swedish kronor.

currency.name: Swedish krona
currency.note: For a euro investor, Swedish shares carry currency risk: moves of the krona against the euro change the value of holdings in euros (Category L).

source.title: FTSE Equity Country Classification Process, v3.5, October 2026, Appendix 3 (FTSE Russell, PDF)

exchanges.name: Nasdaq Stockholm
exchanges.hours: Main market equities 09:00–17:30. In the last five minutes there is no order matching; the closing price is set in a closing auction that ends at a random moment in the final 30 seconds.
exchanges.note: Nasdaq also runs the exchanges in Copenhagen, Helsinki and Iceland, with different hours.

indexes.name: OMX Stockholm 30 (OMXS30)
indexes.description: The 30 largest and most actively traded shares on the Stockholm Stock Exchange; base value 125. Calculated by Nasdaq.

source.title: OMX Stockholm 30 Index overview (Nasdaq Global Indexes)

regulators.name: Finansinspektionen (FI)
regulators.role: The Swedish government authority that monitors the financial market, including banks, insurers and securities markets.

investorProtection.name: Deposit insurance (Riksgälden, Swedish National Debt Office)
investorProtection.text: Since 1 January 2026, deposits are protected up to SEK 1,150,000 per person and institution (the krona equivalent of €100,000, adjusted every five years).

settlement.cycle: T+2 (two business days); T+1 from 11 October 2027
settlement.csd: Euroclear Sweden, the Swedish central securities depository
settlement.note: Like the rest of the EU, Sweden moves to next-day settlement on 11 October 2027.

source.title: One year to go for T+1 settlement (ESMA, 16 October 2026)

rules.title: A and B share classes
rules.text: Many Swedish companies have more than one share class, usually with different voting rights. The OMXS30 itself includes, for example, Atlas Copco A, Volvo B and Investor B (Category C).

source.title: OMXS30 weighting, constituent list (Nasdaq Global Indexes)

rules.title: Short selling (EU rules)
rules.text: Net short positions in shares must be reported to the regulator from 0.1% of issued share capital and published from 0.5% (Category N).

taxes.glance: Non-residents: 30% Swedish withholding tax (kupongskatt) on dividends, reducible under a tax treaty at payment or by refund. Residents: investment savings accounts (ISK) are taxed at 30% of a standard yield instead of on actual gains and dividends.

items.title: Dividends for foreign investors
items.text: The main rule is that 30% withholding tax (kupongskatt) is deducted from dividends. It can be lower if the recipient lives in a country that has a tax treaty with Sweden, either directly at payment or by refund afterwards.

items.title: For an Austrian investor
items.text: An Austrian bank can credit foreign withholding tax only up to 15% of the dividend against Austrian KESt (Category Q); any higher Swedish tax must be reduced or reclaimed in Sweden.

items.title: Residents: investment savings account (ISK)
items.text: In an ISK, gains, dividends and interest are not taxed. Instead, the account is taxed each year at 30% of a standard yield (schablonintäkt) calculated from its value.

sources.title: För dig som betalar svensk kupongskatt på utdelning (Skatteverket, in Swedish)

access: Many Austrian banks and brokers offer trading on Nasdaq Stockholm; check costs for converting euros into kronor.
Indirectly, through funds or ETFs on Swedish or Nordic indexes (Category H).

history.text: The Stockholm Stock Exchange has its first trading day on 4 February.
The deposit insurance limit rises to SEK 1,150,000 on 1 January.

funFacts: The OMXS30 also contains companies headquartered outside Sweden, such as ABB, AstraZeneca and Nordea, which have listings in Stockholm.

sources.title: Euroclear Sweden, the Swedish Central Securities Depository (Euroclear)
